newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-weak - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-weak - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Monday were expected to be mostly steady, in instances $0.50 lower, dealers said.
Weakness was seen in Illinois amid projections for increased hog marketings after the weekend, they said.

Declines also could be fostered by outlooks for continued soft pork prices as wholesale supplies were rebuilt following light production from last week's four-day work schedule due to the Memorial Day holiday, the dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant were seen unchanged at $59.00 per cwt.

Illinois hogs were seen steady to $0.50 lower, with top prices at the plant ranging from $57.50 to $58.00, the dealers said. Indiana/Ohio top prices for hogs shipped to the plant were seen unchanged at $58.50, they said.
Declines could be pared by countervailing ideas that hog movement would remain light and that packers would need to bid higher for their live inventories next week.

Weakness also could be offset as John Morrell and Co.'s hog plant in Sioux Falls, S.D. resumes operation of its second shift, which was temporarily suspended this week, sources said. The added shift could increase competition, they said.
